answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the zenith check immediately, the dawn audit keeps the resolved set and the wharf replay reveals exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 239 aliases thus pays the reading cost 239 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
